subject: Postcall recap — committed inference island and SLA targets
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzales <maria.gonzales@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Postcall recap — committed inference island and SLA targets

Hi Maria — thanks again for the call today. Quick written recap so we have a shared baseline and clear next steps.

TL;DR: Helio Health is asking for a dedicated (single-tenant) inference pool to eliminate noisy-neighbor latency spikes, meet a sustained peak of ~500 req/s (short prompts, median token output ~60), and achieve a p99 latency target <= 200ms for your primary clinical scoring flow. You want a pilot to validate throughput, isolation, and monitoring before committing to a longer reserved contract.

Key pain points you emphasized:
- Latency volatility during morning batch windows (user-facing timeout risk).
- Unpredictable per-token spend from bursty retries and unoptimized batching.
- Compliance need to isolate PHI-processing traffic and produce audit logs for model inference.

Goals we agreed on:
1) Pilot: 3-month reserved pool with isolation (single-tenant) to validate throughput and guardrail metrics.
2) Performance targets: sustain 500 req/s peak, p95 < 80ms, p99 <= 200ms for typical prompt sizes.
3) Cost/quality trade: initial quantization and batching recommendations to reduce token cost with minimal quality impact.
4) Ops: Redwood to provide per-route token breakdowns, tracing hooks, and a runbook for fallback to hosted variants.

Redwood's initial technical proposal (draft):
- Pool sizing: 4x NVIDIA A10G-equivalent GPUs (config for continuous batching + KV cache) as the pilot starting point.
- Isolation: single-tenant pool + optional encrypted KV cache (customer-managed KMS).
- Autoscale/burst: baseline reserved throughput with short-duration burst headroom (up to 40% for traffic spikes).
- SLAs: propose 99.9% availability for the reserved pool; we will provide a draft SLA (attached) with latency SLOs tied to the pilot acceptance criteria.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, p50/p95/p99 latency dashboards, and request-level traces for sampled requests.

Attachments I attached: traffic-snapshot-oct20.csv (your sample), redwood-mop-draft.pdf (ops playbook), helio-sla-ask.xlsx (SLA/acceptance draft).

Proposed next steps / owners:
- Maria: confirm pilot scope (single-tenant vs multi-tenant isolation) and share a 7-day traffic dump (CSV) and procurement contact (who we should loop in).
- Jordan (me): schedule two follow-ups — (a) technical deep dive with Ben (infrastructure) to validate pool sizing and batching, (b) security/compliance checklist with Naomi.
- Ben: propose concrete GPU types and a recommended batching/config matrix for the 4x baseline.
- Naomi: list the minimal SOC2/audit artifacts & timeline for evidence collection.

Timing: can we schedule the technical deep dive on Thu Oct 22 at 10:00 PT? If that doesn't work, suggest two windows.

Acceptance criteria for turning pilot into a committed reservation:
- Pilot meets p99 latency <= 200ms over a 2-week steady-state window and shows predictable per-token spend within the outlined cost envelope.
- Ops/playbook handed over and on-call rotation defined.

If that matches your read, we’ll lock in the 10/22 deep dive, Ben will prepare a first-pass pool-sizing doc, and Naomi will prepare the compliance checklist.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this into a short pilot.
